verseContext: Luke sums up Jesus' whole childhood in one sentence, after telling us that He went home and obeyed His parents.
title: Jesus Grows and Obeys
subtitle: Jesus was a child once too — and He got it right every single day
mainTruth: Jesus lived a whole childhood without ever once disobeying. He did perfectly what none of us manage, and He did it for us.

read.title: Read Together
read.text:
Here is something we do not think about often enough. Jesus was a child.

He was a baby who had to be carried. He was a toddler who had to learn to walk. He was a boy who had jobs to do and a bedtime and a mother who told Him when to come in. He grew taller. He learned things He had not known before. He had a village, and neighbours, and a father who taught Him to work with wood.

And in all of it, He never once did wrong. Not once.

When Jesus was twelve, His family went to Jerusalem for a big festival, along with a huge crowd of cousins and neighbours. When it was over, everybody set off home together, and Mary and Joseph assumed Jesus was somewhere in the group with the other children.

He was not. He was still in Jerusalem.

They went all the way back, and looked for three whole days. Have you ever been lost, or lost somebody? Mary said afterwards how frightened they had been.

And they found Him in the temple, sitting among the teachers — the cleverest men in the country — listening to them and asking them questions. And everybody who heard Him was amazed, because His questions were not a twelve-year-old's questions.

Mary said, 'Why have You done this to us? We have been so worried!'

And Jesus said, 'Did you not know I would be in My Father's house?'

That was the first time anybody heard Jesus say who His real Father was. He knew, at twelve, exactly who He was.

And then — do not miss this part, because it is the whole point — Jesus went home with them to Nazareth. And He obeyed them.

The Son of God, who made the world, spent the next eighteen years being an obedient son in a small town, doing ordinary work, and nobody wrote a single story about it.

Remember King Saul, who did most of what God said? Jesus did all of it. Every day. Every year. That is the obedience none of us has ever managed — and Jesus was doing it for us the whole time.

discuss.title: Talk About It
discuss.question: Jesus was a child once. What did He do every single day?
discuss.parentGuide: The new concept is Jesus' perfect human obedience, and this is the story in the whole curriculum that lands closest to your child's own life. Lean into the ordinary: Jesus had chores, a bedtime, a mother who called Him in, and He got it right every time. Then be careful in two directions. This is not 'so you should obey like Jesus did' — a child who takes that away has heard the law, not the gospel. It is 'Jesus obeyed perfectly, and He did it for you, because you cannot.' Say the second half out loud. And the eighteen quiet years matter: God was pleased with Jesus during years nobody recorded, which is worth a child hearing if they think only visible achievement counts. Retrieve Saul: The King Who Would Not Listen and set the two side by side — most of it, versus all of it.
discuss.familyQuestion: Which ordinary job are we finding hardest right now?

pray.title: Let's Pray
pray.guidedPrayer: Jesus, thank You that You were a child too, and You understand exactly what our days are like. Thank You for obeying perfectly for us, because we cannot. Help us today. Amen.

remember.title: Remember This
remember.memoryVerse: Jesus went home with them, and He obeyed them.
remember.tip: Stand up straight, tap your head, shoulders, knees and toes in turn while you say one word each: 'Jesus — always — obeyed — God.' Speed it up each time.

doToday.title: Do It Today
doToday.action: Do the very next thing a grown-up asks you today straight away, first time, without being asked twice.
doToday.parentNote: Notice it out loud when it happens, and thank Jesus for it in front of them rather than praising the performance. The aim is gratitude for His obedience, not pressure about theirs.
